sentences.text: Me gusta la historia de España.
sentences.translation: I like the history of Spain.
My grandfather knows a lot of stories.

notes: Stem change e → ie: entiendo, entiendes. ¿Entendido? = Got it?
dentro de = inside of; in (dentro de una hora = in an hour).

sentences.translation: I'll be back in an hour.

notes: ¿Qué significa...? = What does ... mean?

sentences.translation: You mean a lot to me.

notes: fin de semana = weekend.

sentences.text: Trabajo cinco días a la semana.
sentences.translation: I work five days a week.

sentences.text: Hace dos semanas que no la veo.
sentences.translation: I haven't seen her for two weeks.

notes: Usually plural: juntos, juntas. junto a = next to.
niña = girl. niños = children.

sentences.text: Los niños están en la escuela.

sentences.translation: The girl is six years old.

sentences.text: De niño, jugaba en la calle.
sentences.translation: As a child, I played in the street.

notes: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon! In Spain also 'early'.

sentences.text: Muy pronto lo vas a saber.

notes: tía = aunt. In Spain, tío / tía is also slang for a guy / girl, or 'mate'.

sentences.text: Mi tío vive en el campo.
sentences.translation: My uncle lives in the country.
My aunt and uncle are coming tomorrow.

sentences.text: Mi tía hace unos pasteles muy buenos.
sentences.translation: My aunt makes really good cakes.
Dude, what are you doing here?

notes: ¡Buena suerte! = Good luck! tener suerte = to be lucky.

sentences.translation: I live in a small city.

notes: Almost always in ni siquiera = not even.

sentences.translation: He didn't even look at me.
I don't even know her name.

sentences.text: No tengo ni siquiera un minuto.
sentences.translation: I don't even have a minute.

notes: ¡Feliz cumpleaños! = Happy birthday!

sentences.translation: I want you to be happy.
I'll be there in five minutes.
I only have a few minutes.

notes: Agrees with the noun: ¿cuántos años? ¿cuánta gente?

sentences.translation: How many brothers and sisters do you have?

sentences.text: ¿Cuántas veces te lo tengo que decir?
sentences.translation: How many times do I have to tell you?

notes: Object pronoun for vosotros, used in Spain. Latin America uses les / los.

sentences.translation: I love you all very much.

sentences.text: La muerte de su padre fue un golpe.
sentences.translation: His father's death was a blow.

sentences.text: Es cuestión de vida o muerte.
sentences.translation: It's a matter of life or death.

notes: dejar de + infinitive = to stop doing. Déjame = let me / leave me.

sentences.translation: I left the keys at home.

sentences.text: Mi padre no me deja salir.
sentences.translation: My father doesn't let me go out.

notes: en realidad = actually.

sentences.translation: Actually, I don't want to go.

notes: Irregular: doy, di, dio. Dame = give me.

sentences.translation: What are you giving your mother?

sentences.text: Mi abuela me dio un regalo.
sentences.translation: My grandmother gave me a present.

notes: Also a term of endearment: ¡Corazón! = Sweetheart!

sentences.translation: Thank you from the bottom of my heart.

notes: tener miedo = to be afraid.
jefa = female boss.

sentences.translation: I talked to the boss yesterday.

notes: Feminine, but el agua (el before a stressed a-): el agua fría.

sentences.translation: Can you give me a glass of water?

notes: no es justo = it's not fair. As an adverb: justo ahora = right now.
esposa = wife. esposos = husband and wife.

sentences.text: Los esposos viven en el centro.

notes: Feminine although it ends in -o: la mano.
¡Ojo! = Watch out!
¡Adelante! = Come in! / Go ahead!

sentences.text: De ahora en adelante, llega temprano.

notes: Stem change o → ue: encuentro, encuentra.

sentences.text: Son las cinco de la tarde.

notes: Before a masculine noun: ningún (ningún problema). When it comes after the verb, put no before the verb: No tengo ninguna pregunta.

sentences.translation: You have something on your face.

sentences.text: Hay caras nuevas en la oficina.
sentences.translation: There are new faces in the office.

notes: ¡Cuidado! = Careful! / Watch out! tener cuidado = to be careful.
Opposite: alto. As a preposition, bajo means 'under': bajo la mesa.

sentences.text: Mi hermano es más bajo que yo.
sentences.translation: My brother is shorter than me.

notes: cerca de = near (to).
Also a noun: un viejo = an old man.
Before an adjective it means 'quite': bastante bien = quite well.
por fin = finally. fin de semana = weekend.

sentences.translation: What are you doing this weekend?

sentences.text: Es el fin de la historia.
sentences.translation: It's the end of the story.

notes: ¿Qué vas a tomar? = What will you have (to drink)? Toma = here you go.

sentences.translation: Do you want to have a coffee?

sentences.text: Tomamos el tren de las ocho.
sentences.translation: We took the eight o'clock train.

sentences.text: Siempre tomo agua con la comida.
sentences.translation: I always drink water with meals.

notes: lo único = the only thing.

sentences.translation: It's the only thing I want.

notes: Escucha = listen (command). Takes a direct object: escuchar música.
en punto = on the dot (a las tres en punto).

sentences.text: Llego a las ocho en punto.
sentences.translation: I'll arrive at eight o'clock sharp.

notes: With an accent in direct and indirect questions (¿Cuándo vienes? / No sé cuándo vuelve). Without an accent, cuando = when, joining two clauses (Cuando llego, te llamo).

sentences.translation: I don't know when he's coming back.

gloss: to keep (doing), to continue; to follow
notes: Irregular: sigo, sigue, siguió. seguir + -ndo = to keep doing: sigue lloviendo.
Past: llegué (with -gu-).

sentences.translation: What time do you get here?

sentences.text: El tren llega a las nueve.
Es fácil, incluso para un niño.
sentences.translation: It's easy, even for a child.

notes: doctora = female doctor. Also médico.

sentences.translation: I have to go to the doctor.

sentences.text: La doctora llega a las diez.

sentences.translation: Although she's tired, she keeps working.
I'll go with you, even though I don't want to.

sentences.text: Es bueno, aunque un poco caro.
sentences.translation: It's good, although a bit expensive.

notes: Common in Spain; in Latin America carro or auto.

sentences.text: Hay muchos coches en la calle.
sentences.translation: There are a lot of cars on the street.
What kind of person are you?

sentences.text: Mi hermano pequeño tiene diez años.
Cuando era pequeña, vivía en el campo.
sentences.translation: When I was little, I lived in the country.

notes: llamarse = to be called: Me llamo Ana = My name is Ana.

sentences.text: Mis padres me llaman cada domingo.
sentences.translation: My parents call me every Sunday.

notes: más allá = further. Like allí, but less exact.
por última vez = for the last time.

sentences.translation: These last few days were hard.

sentences.text: Los vecinos de arriba hacen mucho ruido.
sentences.translation: The upstairs neighbors make a lot of noise.

notes: la Tierra = the Earth (the planet).

sentences.text: Los niños juegan en la tierra.
sentences.translation: The kids are playing in the dirt.

sentences.text: Mi abuelo estuvo en la guerra.
sentences.translation: My grandfather was in the war.

notes: Me da igual = I don't care. In Spain, igual can mean 'maybe': igual viene.
Also a noun: un loco = a madman.
dar una vuelta = to go for a walk or a drive. de vuelta = back. a la vuelta = on the way back / around the corner.

sentences.text: Te lo cuento a la vuelta.
sentences.translation: I'll tell you when I get back.

notes: yo trabajo = I work (trabajo is also the noun 'work, job').

sentences.translation: I don't have to work today.

notes: Also a form of jugar: yo juego = I play.

sentences.text: Me gustan los juegos de mesa.

sentences.translation: What are the rules of the game?

sentences.text: El agua es buena para el cuerpo.
sentences.translation: Water is good for the body.

notes: Replaces y before a word that starts with the sound i: padre e hijo.

gloss: to go in, to come in, to enter
notes: entrar en / a = to go into.

sentences.text: Entramos por la puerta de atrás.
sentences.translation: We went in through the back door.
There are lots of opportunities here.
Can I have your phone number?

notes: al final = in the end. As an adjective: la parte final = the final part.

sentences.translation: In the end, everything turned out fine.

sentences.text: Está al final de la calle.
sentences.translation: It's at the end of the street.

notes: estar listo = to be ready. ser listo = to be clever.

sentences.translation: Did you go to the party?

sentences.text: Mañana hay una fiesta en casa.
sentences.translation: There's a party at home tomorrow.

notes: Common in Latin America. In Spain: coche.

sentences.translation: Where did you leave the car?

sentences.text: Hay dos autos en la puerta.
sentences.translation: There are two cars out front.

notes: yo vivo = I live (vivo is also the adjective 'alive').

sentences.translation: I want to live in the country.

sentences.text: Vivimos aquí desde hace un año.
sentences.translation: We've lived here for a year.

notes: lo antes posible = as soon as possible.

sentences.text: Me voy el mes que viene.

sentences.translation: I've been here for three months.

notes: tener la culpa = to be to blame. Es culpa mía = It's my fault.

sentences.text: Mis hijos van a la escuela.

sentences.translation: We went to the same school.

sentences.text: En el pueblo hay dos escuelas.
sentences.translation: There are two schools in the village.

notes: Also an adverb: habla más fuerte = speak louder.
Refers to an idea, not a thing: por ello = because of that. More formal than eso.

sentences.translation: I don't want to talk about it.
We're going to work on it.

notes: hacer una pregunta = to ask a question.

sentences.translation: Can I ask you a question?
I have a lot of questions.

notes: ¡Atrás! = Get back!
Before a masculine singular noun it becomes mal: un mal día.

sentences.text: El capitán habla con el equipo.
sentences.translation: The captain is talking to the team.
Who is the captain of the ship?

sentences.text: Los dos capitanes se dan la mano.

notes: el bebé or la bebé, depending on the baby.

sentences.translation: We're going to have a baby.

notes: As a noun, un segundo = a second (of time).

sentences.translation: I live on the second floor.
I'll give you a second chance.

notes: mi hermano mayor = my older brother. una persona mayor = an elderly person.

sentences.text: Mi hermana mayor vive en Madrid.
sentences.translation: My older sister lives in Madrid.

notes: In Spain also lunch.

sentences.translation: We don't have any food at home.

sentences.text: Me gusta la comida de mi madre.
Es la comida más importante del día.
sentences.translation: It's the most important meal of the day.
I eat three meals a day.

notes: Stem change o → ue; past murió. morirse de hambre = to be starving.

sentences.text: Su perro murió el año pasado.
Las flores se mueren sin agua.
